method: Scratch Python script shuffled case order and independently randomized A/B per pair using SystemRandom; model names and timing metadata hidden. All 21 judgments written before reading the key. No model calls.
blindingLimits: The task brief disclosed aggregate scores and the occupation failure before the read.
File-format inspection exposed Ember’s first Salesforce output before randomization; that pair was judged a tie.
decision: Switch default to meta/muse-ember; anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 then openai/gpt-6-luna as fallbacks.
rationale: Ember is at least as good on all pairs, avoids the occupation error and has lower measured onboarding latency; the additional $0.0525 per 1k runs is worthwhile.
scoreInterpretation: Existing deterministic EN/PT means: Ember 10/10, Haiku 9.78/10. The teacher-notes preference is for restrained wording within passing expectations, not a new scored failure: “my biology teacher” supports the student context but does not require it.

latency.source: Saved runs, no new measurements; shared machine with other lanes active.

refusalAssessment.assessment: Recorded filters target phishing/credit-card theft instructions, adversarial padding, device code execution, and hacking an ex’s account. None overlaps the 21 specificity cases; the benign Python instruction injection succeeds. A realistic cybersecurity or device-security onboarding goal could resemble the code-execution refusal, so refusal risk is nonzero. Other-task failures do not establish refusal under the specificity prompt.
refusalAssessment.fallbackLimit: Haiku then Luna retain provider diversity. Refusal followed by fallback adds latency; no new call was made to measure that path or its frequency. The p50 gain applies to this sample, not every onboarding goal.

providerCatalog.ember: Listed with structured output, no_training all and zdr all; no deprecation/shutdown field advertised.
providerCatalog.pricing: Existing gateway-prices.json matches the listed Ember token prices; no price change.
